[b]The Foundation of Vang's Kingdom.[/b]
The manuscript telling the foundation of the Vang's Kingdom is very preseved,only small damages on edges and humidity marks.
The manuscript is, many,made with bamboo swollen in black ink.
[i]In the year 779 AEF(1241),Vang Gaivou from the eastern hills forged his way into the Longpan course and proclaimed his sovereignty over entire Longpan's course[edge damage] 
Three dozens of thousands men from hills to conquer the course of Longpan,the local clan ruling,Louv clan and their leader,chief Louv Vaiv,tried to fight[humidty damage],after the battle of the sobbing herons[non legible word] lasted 3 days, Vaiv tried surrender,Gaizou rejected, family of Vaiv[humidity again] dispersed.
As victory, Gaivou made a new shrine in the House of Serenity and Harmony(The Palace of Npaidi)for his victory.
[Edge damaged] year after the foundation,Gaivou ordered offerings in gold and gold papers to be thrown in the Longpan. In 2 years after the foundation Daov Chaw rebelled in south, general Xyoj Bouj superesed in less than two months the bandits. 4 years after his ascension,ordered a expedition to northern islands,however he died before p-[edge damage].

[/i]
[b]Manuscript 2 of the Vang's Kingdom history.[/b]
[i]Vang Thao, youngest brother of Gaivou,which age was 22 when his brother died,was popular among the court,but the local regional lord's preferred his elder brother, Tou, lord of Heguej and for 3 years, the Kingdom remained kingless.[/i]
[i][damage word]-Ue Yeng,took Lord Thao from east to bring him and enthronize in Npaidi.
Lord of Heguej made the unwise decision to stay in his province,decided the new capital would be Tsuaniv, Xyoj Bouj was the one who was ordered to invade and end with Tou in the year 786.
After besieging Tsuaniv for a long month,the rebellious brother retired and put Kue Li to defend,the tired soldiers and officers however,betrayed him and brings to [...Ue]Yeng, who in name of Vang Thao decided to exile him,his officers were properly either integrated or dispersed along the Kingdom without their titles or land,under the name of Louv Gong,Tou lived on west as fisherman.
It was King Thao who made the first official erudite keejs to exist,the court historians they were originally, thanks to King Thao you are reading this manuscript made by myself honoured carrier of ancient memories.
 the historians already existed, but it was  King Thao and Yeng the ones who made it a official prestigious position in the Kingdom, the first Chaw Kevs(Libraries) were in Npaidi,but later expand into the Kingdom.
[/i]
The lower part of the manuscript seems bitten off by bugs, only senseless words remain:
[i]King Thao...tus-...Ua...[/i]
A single passage seems...off,seems as a written much time after,with different style,more scribled but the most legible of the bottom,it says:
"I made it here and will guide[seems erased intentionally]-Ue Fajtse! 
[b]Third Manuscript of Vang's Kingdom[/b].
[i]On the 6th year of King Thao,the river retreated and rain ceased for what seemed no stopable drought,the most renowed shamans were called for a diet in Npaidi court,the idea was to offer a great sacrifice in food for the spirits if the river,only there the drought would stop and rains continue.
[Particularly weak ink do not allow to read]...next year,the drought stopped with a great rains, chancellor Yeng went to the plaza declare the king sacrifice was what made the spirits have mercy and allow the rains come once again,he declared the spirits of waters blessed the kingdom for the next centuries to come.
On same year king Thao made more powerful clans leaders pay bigger tributes,this led to a revolt from Fangz Kue and Zha Chue,which had nothing in common,but refused to pay tribute from a man of mines, the Brief kingdom of Thoj(which name meaning is literally flee, likely depreciative name for their revolt),the king ordered Faw Nplooj and Louv Zha and Xyoj Bouj to superess the revolt.
Instead of fighting, the choose to ran into the south,next to the river course, the battle of red tide(which name was given because was time when red algae grown at most) happened and the clash ended with Louv Zha burning the rebels suplies and making them fall into hunger until surrender, King Thao ordered their leaders to have their titles removed and they be executed,their kids taken to the court to serve as keejs which the chancellor raised as his own kids.
After three years the chancellor gotten ill [damaged words]died, a great grief was made and he was buried on the place where the hills face the Longpan, king Thao rejected eating for 7 days, then returned to rule, but this death affected him[damaged]...
The next chancellor, Kong Daojou did not shared the previous leadership,but was great keej who made the libraries expand,even expanding the history to outside the Vang's influence,sent special keejs to outer neighboring tribes to try study and register them,such tactic was called as naive by king Thao.
In next year,King Thao made a large campaign to conquer western tribes, Kung Kai was their leader, they had over 5 times the size of the kingdom's army,but then Daojou suggested his Majesty to surrender,when the enemy surrender,they would low their guard,and then it happened,but it was the Chancellor who made it,he used his keejs knowledge of the land to convince them he was surrendering and wished for peace, little did they know,it was a trap, and instead the chancellor captured Kung Kai,without a clear proper leader,the tribes get their morale plump,and victory, Kung Kai was allowed to rule autonomously the region conquered until his death,and the chancellor received a award from his Majesty,a  Golden ceremonial axe for his bravery and tactics.[/i]
[b]Fourth Manuscript of the Vang's Kingdom.[/b]
[i]2 years after the victory in west, on 796(1258), a large project was made, Daojou and the Architet Xyoj Zou would make a great library where all knowledge would be inside in [mold marked this part, then it was cleaned,the clean destroyed the location information] made of stone and kept by wooden pillars, King Thao introduced it with a ceremony by burying a collar of his jaded collar as offering for the spirits of the land, "let this place of memories be blessed" he declared.
Around the same year, in half of the year, a Ntsua entourage visited Npaidi,as much King Thao  did not wanted, Doujou insisted his Majesty to study the traditions of the southern people, affirming "a kingdom that is limited to only know about itself, is a kingdom by half."
They came again with masters of tradition to teach about the language and music to the keejs, even bringing peculiar instruments of music, fascinating!"
The Txi neebs declared such instruments apeased the spirits of the winds,and ordered those "flutes" to be buyed.
[Small section seem marked by mold]
[/i]
[b]Fifth.[/b]
Strips of bamboo carved and wrapped in fibers of mulberry tree.
[i][crossed out]-Ue Yeng, of Clan [crossed out]from 786 to 794, adored by King Thao and stabilized the court.
[u]Kong Daojou[/u], of clan Kong from 794 to 818, second ongest serving chancellor, and erudite who expanded the royal libraries.
[U]Zha Paiv[/u], of the Zha clan, but raised by the first chancellor Yeng,he was the one who made the laws and, like his father, reformed, becoming the most trusted man in the late reign of King Thao, his office as chancellor was from 818 to 826.
[u]Lis Vang[/u]of the Lis clan, from 826 to 866, the longest-serving chancellor who nurtured the Kingdom around him.
[i]Vang Hsia[/u], incompetent,apointed by pure nepotism, between 866 and 872.
[u]Xyoj Yu:[/u] a great general,but weak in politics,of the Xyoj Clan, between 872 and 882.
[u]Two Kongs and Two Chengs[/u], between 882 and 899, the Kong clan contested the chancellorship against the Cheng, as the king slowly lost his power and influence. 
The latter part is lost; the last chancellor is mentioned as "Vang Tes", but the part mentioning his chancellorship is also lost, as is its duration, as it dates back to the fall of the Vang's Kingdom in 906/1368.

[/i]
